blocks.text: Two students each dissolve one spoon of salt: one in a cup, the other in a bucket. Both solutions contain the same amount of salt, but only one is worth drinking. Concentration is what separates them, and in the laboratory it has to be a number, not an impression.

blocks.title: Concentration
blocks.text: Concentration is the amount of solute dissolved in a stated volume of solution. Molar concentration is measured in moles per cubic decimetre, mol/dm3, and mass concentration in grams per cubic decimetre, g/dm3. A solution of concentration 1 mol/dm3 is called a molar solution.

blocks.caption: n is moles of solute, V is volume of solution in dm3, M is molar mass in g/mol

blocks.title: Convert cm3 to dm3 first
blocks.text: 1 dm3 = 1000 cm3, so divide any volume in cm3 by 1000 before substituting. Forgetting this step produces answers a thousand times too large or too small and is the single most common error in this topic.

blocks.title: Concentration in both units
blocks.prompt: 5.3 g of anhydrous sodium carbonate is dissolved in water and made up to 250 cm3 of solution. Calculate the concentration in mol/dm3 and in g/dm3. [Na = 23, C = 12, O = 16]

steps.text: Find the molar mass of Na2CO3: (2 x 23) + 12 + (3 x 16) = 46 + 12 + 48 = 106 g/mol.
Convert the volume to cubic decimetres: 250 / 1000 = 0.250 dm3.
Convert to grams per cubic decimetre by multiplying by the molar mass: 0.20 x 106 = 21.2 g/dm3.
Check: 21.2 g in 1 dm3 means 21.2 / 4 = 5.3 g in 250 cm3, which matches the data.

blocks.answer: 0.20 mol/dm3, which is the same as 21.2 g/dm3

blocks.markdown:
## Dilution

Adding water increases the volume but does not change the number of moles of solute. Therefore

$C_1V_1 = C_2V_2$

where subscript 1 is the concentrated stock solution and subscript 2 the diluted one. The volumes can be in cm3 on both sides, since the units cancel.

To make 250 cm3 of 0.20 mol/dm3 solution from a 2.0 mol/dm3 stock:

$V_1 = \dfrac{C_2V_2}{C_1} = \dfrac{0.20 \times 250}{2.0} = 25\ \text{cm}^3$

So measure 25 cm3 of stock into a 250 cm3 volumetric flask and make up to the mark with distilled water.

items: Weigh the calculated mass of solute accurately on a chemical balance
Dissolve it in a small volume of distilled water in a beaker, stirring until no solid remains
Transfer the solution through a funnel into a volumetric flask of the required capacity
Rinse the beaker and funnel with distilled water and add the rinsings to the flask so no solute is lost
Add distilled water until the bottom of the meniscus sits exactly on the graduation mark
Stopper the flask and invert it several times to mix thoroughly

blocks.title: Watch the wording
blocks.text: Concentration is always per volume of final solution, not per volume of solvent added. If a question says a solute is dissolved in 100 cm3 of water and made up to 250 cm3, the volume you use in the calculation is 250 cm3.

points: Concentration in mol/dm3 is moles of solute divided by volume of solution in dm3.
Divide any volume given in cm3 by 1000 before substituting.
Multiply mol/dm3 by molar mass to obtain g/dm3, and divide to go the other way.
On dilution the moles of solute stay constant, so C1V1 = C2V2.
A standard solution is prepared in a volumetric flask and made up exactly to the graduation mark.
